claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase microstructure.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will have superior tribo-corrosion resistance to conventional structural alloys such as duplex stainless steel 2205.
The superior tribo-corrosion resistance arises from the alloy's dual-phase microstructure.
The dual-phase microstructure promotes formation of a protective oxide barrier under high-temperature, mechanically abrasive conditions.
The as-prepared AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy contains FCC and BCC or B2 phases.
Molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 exposure at 450 °C and 650 °C is a relevant corrosive environment for comparing AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with DS2205.
The FCC or FCC-like phase becomes enriched in noble elements.
The FCC or FCC-like phase forms a passivating oxide layer.
The passivating oxide layer shields the more reactive BCC or B2 phase.
The B2 phase in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 undergoes selective dissolution in molten salt because of micro-galvanic coupling between its two phases.
A robust oxide layer minimizes selective dissolution of the less noble phase under combined high-temperature and wear conditions.
The proposed oxide-mediated dual action reduces both electrochemical degradation and mechanical material loss.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a significantly lower molten-salt corrosion rate than DS2205 at 450 °C and 650 °C.
At 450 °C, the reported corrosion rates are approximately 1 mm/year for AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and 8 mm/year for DS2205.
At 650 °C, the reported corrosion rates are approximately 9 mm/year for AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and 20 mm/year for DS2205.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will have lower combined material loss and wear rates than DS2205 under otherwise identical tribo-corrosion conditions.
Extremely aggressive corrosion or wear forces may disrupt the protective oxide layer and eliminate the proposed advantage.
The effect size under combined tribological and corrosive stress has not been quantified by the cited evidence.
Processing variations may influence the proposed protective dual-phase behavior.
